children: Ten NSE shareholders stand to realise about Rs 17,035 crore from the IPO, against an acquisition cost of roughly Rs 534 crore

The selling shareholders of the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. could realise a combined gain of about Rs 16,501 crore from the exchange’s initial public offering, based on the upper end of its price band.

The gains are based on the Rs 1,785 upper price band and the acquisition costs disclosed in NSE’s red herring prospectus. The IPO comprises an offer for sale of about 126.4 million existing shares, with no fresh capital being raised by NSE.
SBI Set To Book Largest Gain

State Bank of India is set to record the largest absolute gain among the selling shareholders. SBI is offering about 15.97 million NSE shares, which it acquired at Rs 0.80 apiece. At the upper price band, the shares are valued at about Rs 2,851 crore, compared with an acquisition cost of roughly Rs 1.28 crore.

Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, or CPP Investments, is offering about 11.87 million shares. Its acquisition cost was Rs 324.13 per share, putting the cost of the shares being sold at about Rs 384.9 crore.

Aranda Investments, a Mauritius-based investor, is offering about 11.25 million shares acquired at Rs 62.38 apiece. The shares are valued at roughly Rs 2,007 crore at the upper band, against an acquisition cost of about Rs 70.2 crore.

MS Strategic (Mauritius), which acquired its 11 million shares at Rs 66.54 apiece, is set to receive about Rs 1,964 crore from the sale at the upper band. Its acquisition cost for these shares was about Rs 73.2 crore.
Institutional Sellers To Realise Large Gains

The New India Assurance Company is offering about 10.5 million shares that it acquired at 32 paise apiece. At Rs 1,785, the shares would be worth about Rs 1,874 crore, compared with an acquisition cost of roughly Rs 33.6 lakh.

SBI Capital Markets is selling about 8.78 million shares acquired at Rs 0.38 apiece. The shares would fetch around Rs 1,567 crore at the upper band, against an acquisition cost of approximately Rs 33.4 lakh.

Bank of Baroda is offering about 7.69 million shares acquired at Rs 0.54 apiece. At the upper price band, the shares are valued at roughly Rs 1,373 crore. Stock Holding Corporation of India is offering about 6.19 million shares, which would be worth approximately Rs 1,104 crore at the same price.

General Insurance Corporation of India is also selling about 6.19 million shares. Its shares, acquired at Rs 5.26 apiece, would generate about Rs 1,104 crore at the upper band, compared with an acquisition cost of around Rs 3.25 crore.

United India Insurance Company is offering about 6 million shares acquired at Rs 0.50 apiece. The stake would be valued at about Rs 1,071 crore at the upper band, against an acquisition cost of roughly Rs 30 lakh.
NSE IPO Offer Size Cut

The number of shares being offered has been reduced from the nearly 149 million shares proposed in NSE’s draft red herring prospectus filed in June to about 126.4 million shares in the final offer documents. The reduction is more than 15 per cent.

SBI has reduced the number of shares it plans to sell, taking the stake on offer to about 0.7 per cent from 1 per cent earlier. SBI Capital Markets has been added as a selling shareholder in the revised offer documents and plans to sell shares equivalent to about 0.35 per cent of NSE.

Other institutional investors have also pared their proposed sales. GIC reduced its proposed sale by 18 basis points, while Bank of Baroda cut its proposed stake sale by 13 basis points, according to the revised offer documents.

The NSE IPO is priced in the Rs 1,700-1,785 range and is scheduled to open on September 17 and close on September 21. At the upper band, the offer values NSE at about Rs 4.42 lakh crore, or roughly USD 46 billion.
As the issue is entirely an offer for sale, NSE itself will not receive proceeds from the IPO. The funds raised will accrue to the existing shareholders selling their shares.
